name: Paladin Oath of Redemption (Paladin Oath)
body:
Paladins that swear an oath of redemption are no less warriors than their peers, but their priorities shift. Instead of slaying evil, they seek to redeem it. Their words can undermine their opponent’s conviction, make them see the errors of their ways and urge them to surrender in ways few threats can. They learn to incapacitate their foes if reason cannot be reached before combat ensues, and always attempt to make the evildoers see the light if doing so wouldn’t jeopardize their other duties.

Code of Conduct: If able to communicate with an opponent, you always have to make an attempt at redemption. Always offer mercy and terms of surrender, and slay only if you’re not able to help the creature without putting others at risk.

Warrior of Mercy (Ex)

At 4th level, an oath of redemption paladin takes no penalty on attack rolls to deal nonlethal damage. If his attack would normally deal additional damage (such as via sneak attack, the flaming weapon special ability, or the like), this additional damage can be nonlethal damage. He can also alter spells with the fire, good, or light descriptors so that the damage they deal is nonlethal damage instead. He must choose if he wants to apply this effect as the spell is cast.

In addition, an oath of redemption paladin is able to use his Diplomacy bonus in place of his Intimidate bonus when making an Intimidate check to demoralize an opponent.

This ability replaces channel positive energy.

Oath Spells

1st—castigate; 2nd—qualm; 3rd—charitable impulse; 4th—atonement.
